gotchas: Authenticate with the x-api-key header: a long-lived API key that works only while its Partner Portal client is active. The docs recommend OAuth2 client credentials instead (POST https://auth.gozem.co/oauth2/token, then Authorization: Bearer; tokens last 3600 s by default). Send one credential per request — if both headers are present, the bearer token is used. Missing or invalid credentials return 401 unauthenticated; an endpoint the client wasn't granted, or a source IP outside its allowlist, returns 403 forbidden. How an API key is issued isn't documented: the Partner Portal flow described only generates a client_id and client_secret — ask your Gozem representative for the key.

vehicle takes the vehicle's guid (VEH_…) or its name, as returned by list_vehicles. The guides disagree on which to send — Getting Started passes the guid, the 'Deliver a package' recipe says to take name, not guid — and only list_vehicles' name filter is documented as case-insensitive: send the value exactly as list_vehicles returns it.

Dropoffs are serviced in the order given unless optimize_route is true, in which case the server reorders them and returns them in delivery order. Each stop needs label, lat and lon; note is at most 280 characters.

A quote is time-limited: book it before expires_at (the recipe says it holds about fifteen minutes) or create a fresh one — booking an expired quote fails with 409 quote_expired. Ask for it when the customer is ready to confirm.

estimated_fare is not a charge until the quote is booked. Don't rely on the breakdown's line items: the recipe says a quote splits the price by cost driver and the invoice per delivery (totals agree), but the Getting Started quote example shows a per-delivery line ('Delivery 1').

vehicle_not_supported (vehicle not recognized), vehicle_not_available (not available at the pickup location) and service_not_available (pickup outside any coverage area) are 400s: fix the request rather than retrying.

This spec lists Togo only: every Courier example is in Lomé. gozem.co lists Togo, Bénin, Cameroun, Gabon and Congo-Brazzaville for the Gozem app, and the developer docs only say 'across West and Central Africa' — whether the Courier API serves the other countries isn't documented. Vehicle availability is per city: check the pickup with list_vehicles (lat/lon) instead of assuming a country or vehicle is served. book_trip's response schema restricts currency_code to XOF.

Sandbox (https://sandbox-api.gozem.co/courier/v1) and production (https://api.gozem.co/courier/v1) are fully isolated: each has its own Partner Portal, API clients, credentials and data, so a sandbox key doesn't work in production. Sandbox carries out no real-world operations and no charges occur, and its data may be reset periodically. A client may only call the endpoints granted to it in the portal, with no implicit access to related routes. Portal access is provisioned during onboarding; the API reference labels the Courier API Beta (spec version 0.0.0).

Failures share one envelope: branch on code — message is human-facing and may be reworded or localized. The API reference describes {success: false, code, message, details}, the API Basics page {error, message, code, details}: read only code, message and details (field-level failures on validation_failed; API Basics types details object, array or null). Statuses listed for this operation: 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 409, 413, 415, 429, 500, 502. Retry only 429 rate_limit_exceeded (honour Retry-After; default limit 100 requests per minute per client; pace with the X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers), 500 internal_error and 502 service_unavailable, with backoff.
